public_rationale: ChatGPT did suffer a conspicuous malfunction. But OpenAI's incident record dates its causal explanation to February 21, before Marcus's February 22 post. The malfunction component holds; “unexplained” does not hold when read as the public state of knowledge at publication.
limitations: The incident was initially unexplained. Reading the adjective as referring only to that initial stage would change the assessment.
OpenAI's explanation is a company account, not an independent technical audit.

statement.excerpt: So let me get this straight? Sora’s can’t reliably handle basic physics, ChatGPT had an unexplained meltdown, Gemini can’t even remember who was on Apollo 11, there are no formal guarantees that any of this will ever work, you yourself admit you don’t know how it works, or how much better it will get next time around, and you want another $7 trillion dollars?
statement.document_title: Belief in magic may be declining

our_interpretation: “Meltdown” means a conspicuous malfunction producing incoherent responses, not a complete outage.
“Unexplained” means no public causal explanation was available when Marcus published on February 22.
The surrounding news context identifies the February 20–21 incident. The target period includes February 22 to assess whether it remained unexplained.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous records establish the malfunction and establish that its cause remained publicly unexplained at publication.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable records disprove the malfunction or show that a public causal explanation preceded the post. If the malfunction occurred but had been explained, the compound claim is mixed.

evidence.excerpt: ChatGPT appears to be encountering serious technical problems that are causing it to provide nonsensical answers to user queries.
evidence.explanation: Documents the conspicuous malfunction described as a meltdown. It supports that component, not continued absence of an explanation on February 22.

evidence.excerpt: On February 20, 2024, an optimization to the user experience introduced a bug with how the model processes language.

evidence.explanation: The event being dated here is publication of the explanation. OpenAI's February 21 update attributed the malfunction to an optimization bug and described incorrect inference-kernel results, preceding Marcus's February 22 post.
